businessProfile.productSummary: High-performance technical outerwear (patroller-grade shells) for serious backcountry skiers.
businessProfile.brandVoice: authoritative, technical, pro-grade — performance-first and durability-focused

reasons: Category match: Cloudfoot is an apparel publisher covering activewear (one of the closest category matches in the catalog).
Audience fit: age skew 25-45 and nearly even gender split (52/47) aligns with typical backcountry skier demographics.
Income/intent: income_tier mid-high and 'tech-adjacent urban professionals' in notes indicate users who buy premium technical gear.
Caveat: publisher avg order value (USD 118) is well below product price, so expect lower on-site conversion but good top-of-funnel awareness.
Category adjacency: Movewell is focused on activewear and fitness apparel (strong overlap with performance clothing buyers).
Audience intent: 'Fitness-engaged shoppers' (age 25-44, income mid-high) are receptive to technical fabric/ performance claims.
Gender skew: heavy female audience (82%) makes this especially useful if the brand targets women skiers or a women's line.
Caveat: low publisher AOV (USD 78) versus product price — likely good for consideration and product education rather than immediate checkout.
Audience & positioning: Stride & Stem targets professional, high-income women with an interest in sustainable apparel — a reachable segment for premium women's ski shells.
AOV & spend: publisher AOV (USD 142) is higher than many apparel pubs here, indicating willingness to purchase higher-ticket apparel.
Messaging overlap: notes around sustainability and quality align if the brand emphasizes materials, durability, and reduced waste.
High-income reach: Northbed's audience is high-income, design-conscious urban/suburban buyers (income_tier: high) who buy big-ticket discretionary items.
Cross-sell signal: notes call out 'high cross-sell with home and wellness' — suggests this audience is comfortable making premium lifestyle purchases outside the publisher's main category.
Use-case: good for reaching affluent buyers as part of a broader lifestyle or gifting push despite being a home publisher rather than apparel-focused.

excludedPublishers.reason: Swiftcart is instant convenience/grocery delivery (AOV USD 28, impulse-driven); shoppers there are not the right place to convert $650+ technical outerwear purchases.
Studiogrid is a wellness services marketplace (fitness classes/spa) focused on bookings, not high-ticket apparel retail.
Marlowe & Co. targets older affluent women with mid-life casual/workwear (96% female, category not focused on technical outdoor performance apparel).
Linden Park skews 50-70 women and sells classic workwear — audience buys premium clothing but the publisher's product focus is conservative/classic rather than technical outdoor gear.
Everbody is focused on plus-size women's intimates and workwear (very strong female representation and fit/size messaging) rather than technical outerwear for backcountry use.
Pawline is a pet category (pet food/supplies), so its shopping intent and category affinity don't match premium ski shells.
Pantrygood is grocery/organic-focused (AOV USD 86) with values-driven food shoppers, not consumers seeking high-ticket technical outerwear.
Ruffco is a large pet retailer audience (pet food/supplies); category mismatch makes it an unlikely place to reach buyers for $650+ ski shells.
Heartfoot sells basics (socks/underwear) with gifting season strengths but low AOV (USD 52) and product mismatch for pro-grade ski shells.
Daily Form focuses on vitamins/supplements (science-forward wellness DTC) — audience intent is health supplements, not premium outdoor apparel purchases.
Velvetline is beauty-focused (skincare/makeup) with a very young, female-skewed audience unlikely to shop for high-ticket backcountry shells on that site.
Hearthstone Goods is specialty cookware/home (AOV USD 198) — while high-income, its shoppers are focused on kitchen/home purchases rather than technical outerwear.
Kitchenly is meal kits (convenience food subscription) with family households; category and shopping intent do not align with premium ski outerwear.
Tailcrate is a pet subscription/toy publisher aimed at millennials treating pets as family, not a destination for $650+ technical apparel.
Strandlab is haircare/personalized beauty with teen/young-adult skew — audience and category don't match premium outdoor gear buyers.
Pop & Sip sells functional beverages (gut health/functional drinks) to a wellness-curious audience; not a likely shopping context for luxury technical shells.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Fitness Enthusiast buys technical, performance apparel and responds to fabric/technical claims; they are likely to value a pro-grade ski shell's performance specifications.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Pro-grade, tested performance — engineered fabrics and construction that perform in extreme, backcountry conditions.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Affluent Classic has the disposable income and preference for quality and longevity; they buy less often but will invest in a premium, durable outerwear piece.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Crafted for longevity — investment-grade construction and materials you can rely on season after season.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Gifter represents high-AOV purchase moments (holidays, life events) where buyers look for impressive, premium products — a $650+ shell fits that remit.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: An impressive, ready-to-gift, professional-grade shell — premium presentation and expedited shipping available for gift occasions.

variants.headline: Patroller-grade shells — engineered for extreme backcountry performance
variants.body: Pro-grade shells the patrollers wear — engineered fabrics and construction that perform in extreme backcountry conditions. Built for sustained exertion and layered systems; starts at $650.
variants.rationale: Calls out patroller-grade credibility and engineered fabrics, matching the fitness enthusiast’s demand for proven performance and technical detail.

variants.headline: Investment-grade shell, crafted to last season after season
variants.body: Patroller-grade construction and materials you can rely on season after season. Understated, precision-built outerwear focused on longevity and dependable function; starts at $650.
variants.rationale: Uses understated, quality-forward language emphasizing longevity and craftsmanship that appeals to an affluent buyer who values investment pieces.

variants.headline: Gift-ready patroller-grade shell — premium presentation, expedited shipping
variants.body: Impressive, professional-grade outerwear for serious backcountry skiers. Premium gift presentation, gift wrap, and expedited shipping options available for last-minute gifting; starts at $650.
variants.rationale: Highlights premium presentation and expedited shipping so shoppers can confidently buy a high-value, ready-to-gift technical shell.

bidStrategy.rationale: Considered purchase at ~$850 AOV: bid to a target CPA of 20-35% of order value so first-order economics stay profitable

budget.rationale: $1500/publisher/month floor for statistically useful volume × 4 publishers × 1.5 luxury-tier multiplier

assumptions: CPMs are heuristic estimates by audience income tier, not quoted rates
Estimated AOV of $850 inferred from the advertiser's description
